title: A 2004 step in the deep-minus-shallow GCMT delay gap was unresolved after trend adjustment in 1990-2020
abstract: We tested whether the deep-minus-shallow centroid-delay gap had a distinct step in 2004, when GCMT changed its analysis method. We used 486 Mw 6.5 to below 7.5 events from 1990-2020 in ten 20-degree cells with both depth groups in both eras. Deep events had centroid depths of at least 300 km. Shallow events had depths below 70 km. Signed delays were scaled to Mw 7 with a cube-root moment rule. A model with cell-by-depth effects, year effects, magnitude bins, fault class and a depth-specific linear trend gave a 2004 step of +1.31 scaled seconds. The conditional 95% spatial cluster interval was -1.73 to +4.34 seconds. Without the depth-specific trend the estimate was -1.19 seconds, with limits of -2.68 to +0.31. Ten-degree cells gave a negative point estimate. The evidence does not resolve a distinct 2004 step or its cause. This extends a prior era comparison on overlapping catalog records. Few spatial clusters, a selected population, trend assumptions and systematic catalog errors limit the result. Code, aggregate results, an independent numerical check, source hashes and a figure are included. External event records are excluded.

display.caption: The 2004 step estimate changes sign with trend and cell choices. Bars show conditional 95% intervals. The right panel uses the same 486 events for each assumed step year. These intervals do not form a breakpoint confidence set.
